requirements.text: wakeup::evaluate_wake_source_signals returns a WakeSourceSignals whose fired mask equals config.wake_enable bitwise-AND observed, WakeSourceSignals::any_fired is true only when that mask is nonzero, and the function never panics for any input

requirements.title: WakeupFunctionalConfig defaults to no armed pins and its layer tag matches crate::regmap's EndpointType::Wakeup cross-layer rule
requirements.text: wakeup::WakeupFunctionalConfig::default().trigger is WakeupTriggerConfig::default(); WakeupFunctionalConfig::layer_tag produces a crate::regmap::PerEpTypeFunctionalConfig tagged EndpointType::Wakeup that satisfies crate::regmap::check_functional_config_matches_ep_type against a generic PerEpConfigBlock of the same ep_type, and is rejected by functional_config_matches_ep_type against a mismatched ep_type

requirements.title: request_sleep_via_sleep_cmd composes a decoded SleepCmdRequest with crate::powerstate::try_enter_power_mode without duplicating its transition or gate logic
requirements.text: wakeup::request_sleep_via_sleep_cmd(SleepCmdRequest, from, to, gate) returns exactly what crate::powerstate::try_enter_power_mode(from, to, gate) returns for every sampled (from, to, gate) combination, and never panics
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.3 ("To bring the RC Server implementation into sleep mode the RC Client has to send a specific request to the WakeUp endpoint."), TC18.txt L4546-4547

requirements.title: wake_source_signals_trigger_handshake composes a fired WakeSourceSignals with crate::powerstate::send_wakeup_request, rejecting when nothing fired
requirements.text: wakeup::wake_source_signals_trigger_handshake returns Err(RcpError::RequestRejected) when WakeSourceSignals::any_fired is false regardless of handshake state, and otherwise delegates to crate::powerstate::send_wakeup_request(state), advancing WakeUpHandshakeState::Idle to RequestSent and rejecting every other starting state; never panics for any input

requirements.title: FragmentReassemblyBuffer::new and fragmentation_supported reflect the rx_stream_max_request_size sentinel
requirements.text: fragment::FragmentReassemblyBuffer::new(0) constructs successfully but fragmentation_supported() returns false; any nonzero bound makes fragmentation_supported() true; a newly constructed buffer is not in_progress and has no segments

requirements.title: accept_fragment rejects every fragment on a fragmentation-unsupported stream
requirements.text: fragment::FragmentReassemblyBuffer::accept_fragment on a buffer constructed with rx_stream_max_request_size == 0 always returns Err(RcpError::UnsupportedCmd), regardless of the fragment's own ms/segment_num, and leaves the buffer not in_progress

requirements.title: accept_fragment enforces a strictly-incrementing, zero-based segment_num sequence
requirements.text: fragment::FragmentReassemblyBuffer::accept_fragment accepts a fragment only when its ByteMessageInfo::read_size_segment_num.as_segment_num() equals the buffer's own next-expected value (starting at 0 and incrementing by 1 per accepted fragment); a gap, duplicate, out-of-order, or non-zero first value returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) and leaves the buffer's prior state unchanged

requirements.title: accept_fragment enforces the rx_stream_max_request_size combined-payload bound
requirements.text: fragment::FragmentReassemblyBuffer::accept_fragment returns Err(RcpError::PayloadTooLarge) and leaves the buffer's prior state unchanged whenever accepting the fragment would push the train's combined payload length past the configured rx_stream_max_request_size, and accepts a fragment landing exactly at that bound

requirements.title: accept_fragment reports Continuing/Complete by ms, and combined_payload matches CombinedFragmentPayload::assemble
requirements.text: fragment::FragmentReassemblyBuffer::accept_fragment returns Ok(FragmentAcceptOutcome::Continuing) when ByteMessageInfo::ms is true and Ok(FragmentAcceptOutcome::Complete) when it is false, including for a single-fragment train; combined_payload() after any sequence of accepted fragments equals crate::e2e::CombinedFragmentPayload::assemble of the same segments in arrival order
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 ("ms 0b – the fragment sequence is completed with this ABB message / 1b - more data to follow in one or more subsequent ABB messages"), TC18.txt L1233-1234

requirements.title: reset clears buffer state for a new train, and a completed buffer rejects further fragments until reset
requirements.text: fragment::FragmentReassemblyBuffer::reset clears is_in_progress, segment_refs, and the segment_num counter back to their construction-time values without changing the configured bound; calling accept_fragment again after a Complete outcome without an intervening reset returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter)

requirements.title: verify_reassembled_train_crc composes check_fragment_crc_placement and crc32_tc18_for_fragment_train against the buffer's own collected segments
requirements.text: fragment::verify_reassembled_train_crc(buffer, header, final_fragment, crc_present) returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) when crc_present is false (the final-fragment CRC-presence rule), otherwise returns exactly what crate::e2e::crc32_tc18_for_fragment_train(header, final_fragment, buffer.segment_refs()) returns for the same inputs, including propagating Err(RcpError::InvalidSize) for an out-of-range final_fragment header and behaving correctly for an empty (zero-fragment) buffer
requirements.tc18: §13.6 ("Fragmentation, if applied to a message, happens after CRC calculation. So, the CRC is only calculated once and will be transmitted in the last segment."), TC18.txt L4274-4275

requirements.title: accept_fragment never panics across arbitrary payload lengths and segment_num wraparound
requirements.text: fragment::FragmentReassemblyBuffer::accept_fragment never panics for any payload length, including empty payloads, and never panics when the 8-bit segment_num counter wraps past 255 back to 0 during a long-running sequence of accepted fragments

requirements.title: RcServer starts HW_UNCONFIGURED with no root client
requirements.text: RcServer::new constructs a server at RcServerState::INITIAL (HW_UNCONFIGURED), with no root client designated and no endpoints registered, holding the caller-supplied GeneralRegisters as its initial snapshot

requirements.title: RcServer::try_transition delegates to RcServerState::try_transition
requirements.text: RcServer::try_transition updates the server's stored lifecycle state to target on Ok, and leaves it unchanged on Err, mirroring RcServerState::try_transition's own success/failure contract

requirements.title: register_endpoint assigns unique ids and rejects duplicate (stream_id, byte_bus_id) pairs
requirements.text: RcServer::register_endpoint assigns each successfully registered endpoint a fresh, distinct EndpointId, and returns Err(RcpError::EpError) without allocating an id or storing the endpoint when (stream_id, byte_bus_id) is already registered

requirements.title: EP0-addressed requests are gated by check_ep0_access_for_stream
requirements.text: RcServer::handle_abb routes a byte_bus_id equal to ep0::EP0_BYTE_BUS_ID to the General-register EP0 path, reachable from every RcServerState for reads, and rejecting a write from any stream other than the designated root client with Err(RcpError::UnauthorizedAccess)

requirements.title: EP0 read returns the GeneralRegisters snapshot; EP0 write is locked
requirements.text: RcServer::handle_abb answers an EP0 read with the current GeneralRegisters::encode snapshot verbatim; an EP0 write is rejected with Err(RcpError::LockedMemAccess) once past the root-client check, since lifecycle::lock_policy assigns RegisterCategory::General no LockPolicy at all (never writable), for the root client exactly as for any other stream

requirements.title: Device-endpoint requests dispatch through EndpointTable, stream-scoped
requirements.text: RcServer::handle_abb resolves a non-EP0 byte_bus_id through EndpointTable::lookup for the requesting stream_id, returns Err(RcpError::EpNotFound) when no endpoint is registered under that exact (stream_id, byte_bus_id) pair (including when it is registered only under a different stream_id), and otherwise dispatches to the registered Endpoint's read or write

requirements.title: Every RcServer response echoes the request's byte_bus_id
requirements.text: Every AcfAbbMessage response RcServer::handle_abb builds carries response.info.byte_bus_id equal to the request's byte_bus_id and response.info.rsp set true, and passes acf::verify_echo_back against the request

requirements.title: handle_ntscf_frame round-trips a whole on-wire request
requirements.text: RcServer::handle_ntscf_frame decodes an NTSCF-framed ACF_ABB request with avtp::decode_ntscf_frame/acf::decode_acf_abb, dispatches it through handle_abb, and re-encodes the response with acf::encode_acf_abb/avtp::encode_ntscf_frame, never panicking for any input including truncated or arbitrary garbage frames

requirements.title: MockEndpoint::write replaces its buffer wholesale
requirements.text: MockEndpoint::write replaces the endpoint's held buffer with the supplied payload verbatim, and a subsequent MockEndpoint::read of at least that many bytes returns exactly what was last written

requirements.title: MockEndpoint::read never panics regardless of requested size vs. buffer length
requirements.text: MockEndpoint::read never panics for any read_size value, including one exceeding the held buffer's current length or a request against an empty buffer, returning at most as many bytes as are actually held

requirements.title: UdpRcServer dispatches non-discovery requests through RcServer::handle_abb
requirements.text: UdpRcServer::serve_one decodes an inbound NTSCF/ACF_ABB datagram, derives the requesting StreamId from the decoded NTSCF header (not a caller-supplied value), and dispatches any non-discovery-shaped request to crate::mock::RcServer::handle_abb under that StreamId, propagating EP0/lifecycle/register-map gating and EndpointTable-routed device-endpoint dispatch (including Err(EpNotFound) for an unregistered device endpoint) unchanged from RcServer's own contract

requirements.title: UdpRcServer answers discovery reads in any lifecycle state, addressed under the server's own identity
requirements.text: UdpRcServer::serve_one recognizes a discovery::is_discovery_request-shaped request, whether addressed under discovery::DISCOVERY_BROADCAST_STREAM_ID or a real client StreamId, and answers it via discovery::build_discovery_response in every RcServerState, with the response NTSCF frame always addressed under UdpRcServer::local_stream rather than the requester's StreamId
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("An RC Server may receive a \"discovery request\" in any state of the life-cycle and shall send a \"discovery response\" in return."), TC18.txt L2731

requirements.title: UdpRcServer grants/refreshes and rejects discovery-stream configure attempts per discovery.rs's own claim rules
requirements.text: UdpRcServer::serve_one recognizes a discovery::is_discovery_configure_request-shaped request, gates it via discovery::check_discovery_access(..., DiscoveryAccessKind::Configure, ...), and on success grants or refreshes the internally-held claim via discovery::try_claim_discovery_stream, storing the result; a configure attempt from a StreamId other than the current live claimant is rejected with Err(RcpError::UnauthorizedAccess) and the existing claim is left unaffected

requirements.title: UdpRcServer rejects a non-discovery request arriving under the broadcast sentinel StreamId
requirements.text: UdpRcServer::serve_one returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter), without ever reaching RcServer::handle_abb, when a decoded request's NTSCF-header StreamId equals discovery::DISCOVERY_BROADCAST_STREAM_ID and the request is neither a discovery::is_discovery_request nor a discovery::is_discovery_configure_request shape

requirements.title: is_discovery_configure_request recognizes the write-direction discovery shape
requirements.text: is_discovery_configure_request returns true iff msg is a write-direction (op true) ACF_ABB addressed to EP0_BYTE_BUS_ID whose payload's leading DISCOVERY_REGISTER_ADDRESS_LEN bytes decode to DISCOVERY_REGISTER_ADDRESS, is mutually exclusive with is_discovery_request for the same message (differing only in op), ignores trailing payload bytes beyond the register-address prefix, and never panics for any input

requirements.title: NTSCF header golden vector
requirements.text: conformance::golden::NTSCF_GOLDEN_BYTES is a frozen literal byte array whose 12 octets are derived by hand from TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.1 Figure 6 (NTSCF-Header Version 0, p.22) and cross-checked against the worked example in TC18 Figure 20 (p.79), not captured from this crate's own encoder; avtp::encode_ntscf_header(conformance::golden::ntscf_header_fields()) must equal it, and avtp::decode_ntscf_header of it must recover ntscf_header_fields() unchanged
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 6 ("NTSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1130-1138

requirements.title: TSCF header golden vector with non-degenerate avtp_timestamp
requirements.text: conformance::golden::TSCF_GOLDEN_BYTES is a frozen literal byte array for a TscfHeader whose avtp_timestamp is non-zero, whose 24 octets are derived by hand from TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.1 Figure 5 (TSCF-Header Version 0, p.22) and cross-checked against the worked example in TC18 Figure 19 (p.79), not captured from this crate's own encoder; avtp::encode_tscf_header(conformance::golden::tscf_header_fields()) must equal it, and avtp::decode_tscf_header of it must recover tscf_header_fields() unchanged
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 5 ("TSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1121-1128

requirements.title: ACF_ABB message golden vector
requirements.text: conformance::golden::ACF_ABB_GOLDEN_BYTES is a frozen literal byte array; acf::encode_acf_abb(conformance::golden::acf_abb_fields()) must equal it, and acf::decode_acf_abb of it must recover acf_abb_fields() unchanged

requirements.title: ACF_GBB message golden vector with non-zero message_timestamp
requirements.text: conformance::golden::ACF_GBB_GOLDEN_BYTES is a frozen literal byte array for an AcfGbbMessage whose message_timestamp is non-zero; acf::encode_acf_gbb(conformance::golden::acf_gbb_fields()) must equal it, and acf::decode_acf_gbb of it must recover acf_gbb_fields() unchanged

requirements.title: Composed NTSCF+ACF_ABB frame golden vector
requirements.text: conformance::golden::NTSCF_ACF_ABB_FRAME_GOLDEN_BYTES is a frozen literal byte array combining ntscf_header_fields() and the encoded acf_abb_fields() message via avtp::encode_ntscf_frame; its 24 octets are the concatenation of the spec-derived NTSCF_GOLDEN_BYTES (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.1 Figure 6, p.22) and ACF_ABB_GOLDEN_BYTES (TC18 §11.2.1 Figure 7 / Table 4, p.24), with nothing between them because Figure 6 places acf_payload_data immediately after stream_id; encoding must equal it, and avtp::decode_ntscf_frame of it must split back into the original header and ACF_ABB payload bytes

requirements.title: go-RCP interop cross-check divergence is documented and pinned
requirements.text: conformance::go_rcp_crosscheck's byte constants, captured from SoundMatt/go-RCP's avtp/acf packages at commit bdc760fb057f067cfb68199b6c3d0edab9e0c671 for field values logically analogous to the golden vectors, must remain provably non-identical to this crate's own golden vector bytes at the header/message level (documenting the header-length, data-length-field-packing, timestamp-status-marker, message-kind-discriminant, and byte_bus_id-width divergences found), while the stream_id sender-MAC/suffix byte layout must remain identical between the two implementations

requirements.title: finalize_crc_trailer places the CRC32 trailer after pad, matching TC18's real wire order
requirements.text: finalize_crc_trailer(frame, crc), given an already-encoded CRC-free ACF_ABB/ACF_GBB frame built from the real payload alone, bumps that frame's own byte_message_info.acf_msg_length by CRC_TRAILER_QUADLETS (one quadlet) and appends crc's 4 big-endian octets after the encoder's own already-correctly-placed pad octets, producing the wire order header (+ message_timestamp), payload, pad, CRC — never payload, CRC, pad, which is what a caller gets by concatenating payload and CRC bytes into one blob before calling encode_acf_abb/encode_acf_gbb; returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for a frame shorter than the byte_message_info header and Err(RcpError::InvalidSize) when bumping acf_msg_length would overflow its 9-bit field

requirements.title: split_crc_trailer recovers the real payload and CRC from a CRC-protected frame without misreading trailer bytes as pad
requirements.text: split_crc_trailer(frame) un-adjusts byte_message_info.acf_msg_length by CRC_TRAILER_QUADLETS and removes the trailing 4 CRC octets before returning (body, crc), so that acf::decode_acf_abb/acf::decode_acf_gbb's existing pad-stripping logic (which strips exactly byte_message_info.pad octets from the end of the acf_msg_length-described region) correctly recovers the real payload from body instead of misreading the CRC trailer's own bytes as padding; round-trips finalize_crc_trailer's output back to the original real payload and CRC value, and returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame)/Err(RcpError::InvalidSize) for a frame too short to hold a header plus CRC trailer or whose acf_msg_length is smaller than CRC_TRAILER_QUADLETS

requirements.title: Annex J UDP encapsulation sequence number is prepended/stripped correctly
requirements.text: encode_annex_j_udp_payload(seq, avtpdu) prepends seq as 4 big-endian octets before avtpdu with no other framing; decode_annex_j_udp_payload(buf) is its exact inverse, returning (seq, avtpdu_bytes) for any buf of at least 4 bytes and Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for fewer than 4 bytes; ANNEX_J_CONTROL_PORT (17221) and ANNEX_J_CONTINUOUS_PORT (17220) are distinct constants documented as taken from public secondary sources (a Wireshark issue tracker discussion and the COVESA Open1722 reference implementation), not the paywalled IEEE 1722-2016 primary standard text

requirements.title: StdUdpSocket::send_to encapsulates outgoing datagrams with a monotonically increasing sequence number
requirements.text: StdUdpSocket is a real UdpSocket implementation over a bound std::net::UdpSocket; StdUdpSocket::bind/new_default_port construct it against a real OS socket, and every StdUdpSocket::send_to call prepends the current value of a per-instance monotonically increasing u32 counter (starting at 0) via encode_annex_j_udp_payload before writing to the real socket, with no receiver-side semantics (e.g. loss detection) invented or implied for that counter beyond monotonic increase

requirements.title: StdUdpSocket::recv_from strips the Annex J sequence number and maps a real socket timeout to RcpError::Timeout
requirements.text: StdUdpSocket::recv_from applies timeout via the real socket's SO_RCVTIMEO (None blocks indefinitely), strips the leading 4-byte Annex J sequence number from whatever datagram is received via decode_annex_j_udp_payload before returning the remaining AVTPDU bytes to the caller, and maps a real OS-level receive timeout (WouldBlock/TimedOut) to Err(RcpError::Timeout) rather than propagating the raw std::io::Error

requirements.title: ETHERTYPE_AVTP names the real IEEE 1722 EtherType and is placed big-endian in the Ethernet header
requirements.text: ETHERTYPE_AVTP is 0x22F0, matching TC18 §10.1 (“an AVTPDU is marked by an EtherType value of 0x22F0”); encode_ethernet_frame writes it as bytes 12-13 of the frame in big-endian order, and decode_ethernet_frame reads bytes 12-13 the same way when validating a frame's EtherType

requirements.title: encode_ethernet_frame/decode_ethernet_frame round-trip a raw Ethernet II frame with no encapsulation sequence number
requirements.text: encode_ethernet_frame(dest_mac, src_mac, avtpdu) produces dest_mac (6 bytes) || src_mac (6 bytes) || ETHERTYPE_AVTP (2 bytes, big-endian) || avtpdu directly, with no additional framing (unlike crate::udp::encode_annex_j_udp_payload's 4-byte sequence number, which has no L2 counterpart); decode_ethernet_frame is its exact inverse for any well-formed input, returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for fewer than 14 bytes, and returns Err(RcpError::Other(_)) (not a panic) when the EtherType field is not ETHERTYPE_AVTP

requirements.title: L2Socket trait mirrors UdpSocket's testable-abstraction shape for MAC-addressed raw Ethernet frames
requirements.text: L2Socket::send(frame) and L2Socket::recv(timeout) operate on already-framed encode_ethernet_frame/decode_ethernet_frame bytes, the same already-framed-bytes-in-bytes-out contract crate::udp::UdpSocket documents, letting L2Transport be tested against a mock L2Socket with no real socket involved

requirements.title: L2Transport is constructed with a local StreamId, an L2Socket, a caller-supplied destination MAC, and this transport's own source MAC
requirements.text: L2Transport::new(local_stream, socket, dest_mac, src_mac) stores all four; L2Transport::local_stream/dest_mac/src_mac each return exactly the value passed to the constructor; dest_mac may be unicast or multicast and is always a caller input, since this crate does not derive or allocate a multicast MAC of its own

requirements.title: L2Transport::send_acf_abb/send_acf_gbb reject a zero timeout immediately, matching UdpTransport's own discipline
requirements.text: L2Transport::send_acf_abb and L2Transport::send_acf_gbb both return Err(RcpError::Timeout) immediately, without ever calling the underlying L2Socket, when passed Some(Duration::ZERO), mirroring crate::udp::UdpTransport::send_acf_abb's own zero-timeout short-circuit

requirements.title: L2Transport::send_acf_abb/send_acf_gbb build an NTSCF/AVTPDU frame, wrap it as a raw Ethernet frame, and verify the response echoes byte_bus_id
requirements.text: L2Transport::send_acf_abb/send_acf_gbb encode the request via crate::acf::encode_acf_abb/encode_acf_gbb, wrap it in an NTSCF frame via crate::avtp::encode_ntscf_frame under this transport's local_stream, wrap that in a raw Ethernet frame via encode_ethernet_frame addressed to dest_mac from src_mac, send it, decode the received response through decode_ethernet_frame/crate::avtp::decode_ntscf_frame/crate::acf::decode_acf_abb (or decode_acf_gbb), and reject it via crate::acf::verify_echo_back if the response's byte_bus_id does not match the request's

requirements.title: RawEthernetSocket (Linux) binds an AF_PACKET/SOCK_RAW socket to a named interface, reading that interface's own MAC rather than requiring the caller to supply one
requirements.text: On target_os = "linux", RawEthernetSocket::bind(interface_name) opens a real AF_PACKET/SOCK_RAW socket (requiring CAP_NET_RAW or root) and binds it to interface_name, reading that interface's own link-layer address via getifaddrs for RawEthernetSocket::mac() rather than accepting a caller-supplied MAC; RawEthernetSocket::send/recv implement L2Socket over that real socket and round-trip a real Ethernet frame byte-for-byte over a veth pair

requirements.title: RawEthernetSocket exists and fails explicitly, never silently, on every non-Linux target
requirements.text: On any target where target_os != "linux", crate::l2::RawEthernetSocket still exists as a type (so downstream code can reference it unconditionally) but RawEthernetSocket::bind always returns Err(RcpError::Other(_)) explaining that AF_PACKET raw sockets are a Linux-specific facility, rather than silently no-op-ing or panicking

requirements.title: serve --udp <bind-ip> [--port <n>] [--stream <hex>] [--max-requests <n>] runs UdpRcServer over a real StdUdpSocket
requirements.text: The CLI must, when invoked with serve --udp <bind-ip>, bind a real rcp::udp::StdUdpSocket to <bind-ip>:--port (default rcp::udp::ANNEX_J_CONTROL_PORT) and dispatch inbound requests through rcp::udp::UdpRcServer::serve_one against a fresh RcServer, stopping after --max-requests requests have been served if given (default: unbounded, until a fatal socket error), exiting 3 on a bind or fatal serve error

requirements.title: ACF_ABB acf_msg_type discriminant is 0x0E
requirements.text: ACF_ABB_MSG_TYPE is 0x0E, matching TC18 §11.2.1 Table 4 (TC18.txt:1149, "acf_msg_type 0x0E (ABB message)") for requests and TC18 §11.3 Table 15 (TC18.txt:1863, "0x0E - ABB message without message_timestamp") for responses.
requirements.tc18: §11.3 Table 17 ("Usage of ABB/GBB message for responses"), TC18.txt L2242-2266

requirements.title: ACF_ABB and ACF_GBB msg_type constants are distinct, differing only by message_timestamp
requirements.text: ACF_ABB_MSG_TYPE (0x0E) and ACF_GBB_MSG_TYPE (0x0D) are the two acf_msg_type discriminants TC18 §11.3 Table 15 (TC18.txt:1863) defines; the sole structural difference between the two message shapes is the 8-octet message_timestamp field GBB carries and ABB omits.
requirements.tc18: §11.3 Table 17 ("Usage of ABB/GBB message for responses"), TC18.txt L2242-2266

requirements.title: rsv bit-pairs are always encoded as zero and unrepresentable
requirements.text: encode_byte_message_info never sets either rsv bit-pair to a nonzero value, per TC18 §11.2.1 Table 4 (TC18.txt:1153, "rsv 00b") and TC18 §11.3 Table 15 (TC18.txt:1867, "rsv 00b"); ByteMessageInfo has no field through which a caller could set them to anything else.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Table 4 ("Usage of ABB message for standard requests"), TC18.txt L1208-1236

requirements.title: ByteMessageInfo::read_size() is None when op indicates a write
requirements.text: ByteMessageInfo::read_size() returns Some(value) only when op=0 (read, response-with-data expected) and None when op=1 (write), per TC18 §11.2.1 Table 4's own polarity (TC18.txt:1163, "if op = 0 this is read_size, else segment_num", with op semantics at TC18.txt:1160-1161).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Table 4 ("Usage of ABB message for standard requests"), TC18.txt L1208-1236

requirements.title: FrameFormat enum names the six Classical/FD/XL CAN frame formats
requirements.text: FrameFormat enumerates the six named CAN frame formats (Classical/FD standard and extended, XL classical and new PHY) this crate's CAN controller targets; wire-byte assignment is this crate's own working interpretation pending a confirmed spec encoding (see the module's own provenance note).
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 Table 57 ("can frame formats"), TC18.txt L5863-5872

requirements.title: FrameFormat::from_u8 rejects Table 54's two reserved codes without panicking
requirements.text: FrameFormat::from_u8 returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) for any byte outside 0..=5; values 6 and 7 are TC18 §13.7.11.3 Table 54's own two Reserved rows (TC18.txt:5454), and no FrameFormat value wider than 3 bits exists. Never panics for any input.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 Table 57 ("can frame formats"), TC18.txt L5863-5872

requirements.title: CanDataFrame::encode right-aligns an 11-bit CAN ID and never emits an RTR indication
requirements.text: CanDataFrame::encode's big-endian id field right-aligns an 11-bit CAN ID within the CAN ID field, per TC18 §13.7.11.3 (TC18.txt:5471, "In case the CAN ID is 11bits, then it shall be right aligned in the CAN ID field"); no remote-frame (RTR) indication is ever emitted, matching the same line's statement that remote frames are not supported.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 ("In case the CAN ID is 11bits, then it shall be right aligned in the CAN ID field."), TC18.txt L5887

requirements.title: CanDataFrame has no field or variant capable of representing a remote frame
requirements.text: CanDataFrame's fields (a FrameFormat restricted to the four non-XL variants, an arbitration ID, and data bytes) cannot represent a CAN remote frame under any value assignment, matching TC18 §13.7.11.3's statement that remote frames are not supported (TC18.txt:5471).
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 ("Sending remote frames is not supported."), TC18.txt L5887

requirements.title: CAN_XL_MAX_PAYLOAD is 2048 bytes, CAN_XL_SUBHEADER_LEN is 6 bytes
requirements.text: CAN_XL_MAX_PAYLOAD (2048) and CAN_XL_SUBHEADER_LEN (6) match TC18 §13.7.11.3 (TC18.txt:5443, "For CAN XL this can be up to 2054 bytes (2048 + 6)") and TC18.txt:5472's 6-byte RRS/SDT/VCID/AF CAN XL sub-header content.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 ("For CAN XL this can be up to 2054 bytes (2048 + 6, see below), which requires segmentation."), TC18.txt L5859-5860

requirements.title: CanRequest enumerates the decoded shape of a Row-2 CAN request after evt[2:0] validation
requirements.text: CanRequest's two variants (Plain(CanDataFrame), ConfigWrite) give an incoming CAN request's decoded shape after its evt.sub_opcode has been validated against evt_row2_kind_of's Table 33 Row-2 rule; CanRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode is the request-decode entry point that performs that validation and dispatch. Unlike I2cRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode/LinRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode/AdcRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode/PwmInRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode (each of which take raw byte_msg_payload bytes and decode them internally), CanRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode takes an already-decoded CanDataFrame -- CAN's own request payload is either a CanDataFrame (Classical/FD) or a CanXlFrame (XL), selected by the payload's own FrameFormat tag byte, a question this crate's own TC18 reconciliation note already flags as not fully reconciled against TC18 Figure 40's real wire word layout, so this evt[2:0]-classification entry point does not itself guess which decoder to invoke by peeking at raw bytes
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33's Row-2 row (CAN is one of its eight endpoint types), TC18.txt L4085-4092, and §13.7.11.3 CAN EP request handling, TC18.txt L5842-5856

requirements.title: CanRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode accepts Plain, rejects Reserved sub_opcodes with UnsupportedCmd, and rejects ConfigWrite with ConfigWriteNotImplemented, never panicking
requirements.text: CanRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode wraps the caller-supplied CanDataFrame unchanged in CanRequest::Plain for a Plain (sub_opcode 0) request. Every Reserved sub_opcode value (evt[2:0] in 001b..=110b, or any value outside the 3-bit field's representable range) returns Err(RcpError::UnsupportedCmd), matching TC18 Table 33's Row-2 error-code requirement and crate::i2c::I2cRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode's/crate::lin::LinRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode's/crate::adc::AdcRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode's/crate::pwm::PwmInRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode's identical refusal of their own table's reserved code. A ConfigWrite (sub_opcode 7) request returns Err(RcpError::ConfigWriteNotImplemented) rather than Ok(CanRequest::ConfigWrite) -- see REQ-CAN-019 and crate::can's own doc comment 'Provenance note: evt[2:0] request validation' for why this diverges from I2cRequest's/LinRequest's/AdcRequest's/PwmInRequest's own Ok(Self::ConfigWrite) precedent. Never panics for any sub_opcode/frame combination
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("000b to 110b reserved – request to be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD" / "111b: ... used to change the configuration of the endpoint (see 12.7.1)"), TC18.txt L4085-4092

requirements.title: RcpError gains ConfigWriteNotImplemented as a new variant for CAN's own evt[2:0]==111b classification, deliberately distinct from I2C/LIN/ADC/PWM_IN's Ok(ConfigWrite) precedent
requirements.text: RcpError::ConfigWriteNotImplemented is added as a new variant (not collapsed onto UnsupportedCmd, which TC18 Table 33 scopes specifically to the Reserved evt[2:0] range, not the distinct 111b ConfigWrite classification), is distinct from other RcpError variants under equality, its Display text names both the 111b evt value and TC18 §12.7.1, CanRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode constructs it for every evt[2:0]==111b request, capi::CError gains a matching ConfigWriteNotImplemented=29 discriminant with a corresponding From<&RcpError> for CError arm, and it is kept out of both is_tc18_error_code's eleven-member group and tc18_wire_code's Table 27 mapping (returning None), matching ChainAborted/ChainError/CrcError's own precedent for crate-synthesized, non-TC18-numbered variants
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33's 111b Row-2 cell (TC18.txt L4085-4092) reconciled against §12.7.1 (functional-config write) and Table 30's own 17-code error list (TC18.txt L3812-3844), which names no dedicated code for "config-write recognized but not yet decodable"

requirements.title: RequestKind::Standard's discriminant carries materially lower confidence than the other eight
requirements.text: RequestKind's doc comment explicitly flags that RequestKind::Standard's numeric wire value is this crate's own working assumption rather than a spec-confirmed encoding, unlike the other eight discriminants (compound/compound-wait/triggered/chained/timed/cancel variants) which trace to specific TC18 Table 5-13 citations.

requirements.title: CRC32_TC18_POLY_REFLECTED is the bit-reversed form of TC18's CRC32P4 polynomial
requirements.text: CRC32_TC18_POLY_REFLECTED (0xC8DF352F) is the standard reflected-CRC bit-reversal of TC18 §13.6 Table 31's "CRC32P4" polynomial 0xF4ACFB13 (TC18.txt:3792), independently cross-checked by tests::crc32_tc18_reference against the unreversed form.
requirements.tc18: §13.6 Table 34 ("CRC32 Polynomial"), TC18.txt L4193-4208

requirements.title: build_crc32_coverage_buffer covers requests and responses via the identical scheme
requirements.text: build_crc32_coverage_buffer and crc32_tc18 have no direction parameter; a response's covered bytes differ from a request's only via the rsp/err/evt bits already present inside the covered byte_message_info, per TC18 §13.6 (TC18.txt:3808, "The CRC calculation for request and response follows the identical scheme").
requirements.tc18: §13.6 ("The CRC calculation for requests and responses follows the identical scheme."), TC18.txt L4276

requirements.title: build_crc32_coverage_buffer is shared by both request and response encoding paths
requirements.text: Both request-side and response-side CRC coverage go through the same build_crc32_coverage_buffer/crc32_tc18 pair with no direction-specific branch, per TC18 §13.6's identical-scheme rule (TC18.txt:3808).
requirements.tc18: §13.6 ("The CRC calculation for requests and responses follows the identical scheme."), TC18.txt L4276

requirements.title: build_discovery_request matches Table 16 except the acknowledged op-bit spec typo
requirements.text: build_discovery_request matches TC18 §12.6 Table 16's discovery-request field values, except that Table 16's own op row ("1b (read request)") contradicts both TC18.txt:3207's general op=0-means-read rule and this crate's implementation; the mismatch is treated as a specification typo, not implemented as written.
requirements.tc18: §12.6.1 ("op 1b (read request)"), TC18.txt L2756

requirements.title: build_discovery_response matches Table 17 except two disclosed, separately-tracked gaps
requirements.text: build_discovery_response matches TC18 §12.6 Table 17's discovery-response construction (RC Server's register map content starting from address 0x00000), except: response length is not clamped to the discovery request's read_size (TC18.txt:2422, tracked as REQ-DISC-029) and no stream_id is built by this function at all (Table 17's stream_id = localMAC + unique_id 0x0000 row, tracked as REQ-DISC-030) -- both gaps are recorded, not silently absorbed.
requirements.tc18: §12.6.2 ("The RC Server will respond with the part of the RC Server’s register map as starting from 0x0000 and its length being determined by the read_size in the discovery request"), TC18.txt L2778-2779

requirements.title: EndpointType::to_u8 matches TC18 Table 29's ep_type values exactly
requirements.text: EndpointType::to_u8 produces exactly the ep_type byte TC18 v0.5.1_RC §13.2 Table 29 ("ep_type values", p.73) assigns to the same endpoint type, for every EndpointType variant.
requirements.tc18: §13.2 Table 32 ("ep_type values": 0x00 Server(EP0), 0x01 WakeUp, 0x02 GPIO, 0x03 SPI, 0x04 I2C, 0x05 UART, 0x06 LIN, 0x07 PWM_OUT, 0x08 PWM_IN, 0x09 ADC, 0x0A DAC, 0x0B CAN, 0x0C ISELED, 0x0D MDIO), TC18.txt L4000-4017 -- note: this requirement's own text cites this as "Table 29" at p.73, a stale table/page number: in the current TC18.txt (RC5), Table 29 is "Execution procedure" (a different table); the actual ep_type enumeration is Table 32 at p.83

requirements.title: tc18_wire_code maps every mappable RcpError to its correct Table 27 numeric value
requirements.text: RcpError::tc18_wire_code returns the exact TC18 §12.9.6 Table 27 numeric value for every error variant that has one: UNSUPPORTED_CMD=1, SEQUENCER_NOT_KNOWN=2, UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS=3, LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS=4, REQUEST_CANCELED=5, REQUEST_NOT_FOUND=6, EP_ERROR=7, EP_NOT_FOUND=8, PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL=9, REQ_STORAGE_OVFL=10, REQUEST_REJECTED=11, POCI_FAILURE=12, PRESENTATION_TIME_TOO_FAR=13, GPTP_FAIL=14, INVALID_PARAMETER=15, CHAIN_ABORTED=16, CHAIN_ERROR=17.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.6 Table 30 ("Error codes in responses": UNSUPPORTED_CMD=1, SEQUENCER_NOT_KNOWN=2, UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS=3, LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS=4, REQUEST_CANCELED=5, REQUEST_NOT_FOUND=6, EP_ERROR=7, EP_NOT_FOUND=8, PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL=9, REQ_storage_OVFL=10, REQUEST_REJECTED=11, POCI_FAILURE=12, PRESENTATION_TIME_TOO_FAR=13, GPTP_FAIL=14, INVALID_PARAMETER=15, CHAIN_ABORTED=16, CHAIN_ERROR=17), TC18.txt L3812-3842 -- note: this requirement's own text cites this as "Table 27", a stale table number: in the current TC18.txt (RC5), Table 27 is "Responder QUEUE_config" (a different table); the actual error-codes table is Table 30

requirements.title: tc18_wire_code covers all seventeen Table 27 codes, not a subset
requirements.text: RcpError::tc18_wire_code's match arms cover all seventeen real TC18 Table 27 error codes (§12.9.6), including the four codes (PwmInNoSignal, PociFailure, PresentationTimeTooFar, GptpFail) a naive reading might expect to be missing.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.6 Table 30 ("Error codes in responses": UNSUPPORTED_CMD=1, SEQUENCER_NOT_KNOWN=2, UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS=3, LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS=4, REQUEST_CANCELED=5, REQUEST_NOT_FOUND=6, EP_ERROR=7, EP_NOT_FOUND=8, PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL=9, REQ_storage_OVFL=10, REQUEST_REJECTED=11, POCI_FAILURE=12, PRESENTATION_TIME_TOO_FAR=13, GPTP_FAIL=14, INVALID_PARAMETER=15, CHAIN_ABORTED=16, CHAIN_ERROR=17), TC18.txt L3812-3842 -- note: this requirement's own text cites this as "Table 27", a stale table number: in the current TC18.txt (RC5), Table 27 is "Responder QUEUE_config" (a different table); the actual error-codes table is Table 30, and all seventeen codes are confirmed present

requirements.title: RequestKind::from_u8 rejects any non-discriminant byte without panicking
requirements.text: RequestKind::from_u8 returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) for any byte value other than the type's named discriminants (compound/triggered/chained/timed/cancel/priority/safety/standard variants); never panics for any input.

requirements.title: Evt::sub_opcode models evt[2:0] per TC18 §13.5's request-direction reading
requirements.text: Evt::sub_opcode models TC18 §13.5's request-direction description of evt[2:0] ("evt[2:0] are used to control the usage of the byte_msg_payload"), distinct from the response-direction whole-nibble reading TC18 §11.3 Table 15 assigns the same four bits (tracked separately as REQ-RESP-004).
requirements.tc18: §13.5 ("event bits evt[2:0] are used to control the usage of the byte_msg_payload."), TC18.txt L4069-4071

requirements.title: Evt::ack models evt[3] as the request-direction acknowledge-request bit
requirements.text: Evt::ack models TC18 §13.5's evt[3] ("evt[3] is used to request an acknowledge. I.e. evt[3]=1 requests acknowledge"), a request-direction reading distinct from the response-direction whole-nibble reading of the same four bits TC18 §11.3 Table 15 defines (tracked separately as REQ-RESP-004).
requirements.tc18: §13.5 ("evt[3] is used to request an acknowledge. I.e. evt[3] = 1 requests acknowledge."), TC18.txt L4072

requirements.title: GPIO_BITMASK_LEN is 4 bytes, matching a 32-IO endpoint
requirements.text: GPIO_BITMASK_LEN is 4 bytes (32 bit positions), matching TC18 §13.7.4.1's "Each GPIO endpoint can handle up to 32 IOs".
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.1 ("Each GPIO endpoint can handle up to 32 IOs"), TC18.txt L4789

requirements.title: GpioBitmask::encode's big-endian byte order matches Figure 24's bit layout
requirements.text: GpioBitmask::encode's big-endian encoding places IO0 in the last byte's least-significant bit and IO31 in the first byte's most-significant bit, matching TC18 §13.7.4.1 Figure 24's payload layout (msb on the left) for its own 24-pin worked example.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.1 Figure 25 ("GPIO request (example for EP with 24 pins)") -- note: this crate's own text/doc-comments call it "Figure 24", a stale figure number from an earlier TC18 revision; the current TC18.txt (RC5) numbers it Figure 25, TC18.txt L4806-4808

requirements.title: GpioWriteSemantics::Or with an all-zero operand is a documented no-op
requirements.text: apply_gpio_write with GpioWriteSemantics::Or and an all-zero operand leaves the current value unchanged for every current value (OR-with-zero is the identity), matching TC18 §13.7.4.3's worked example ("A request with data '0x0000 0000' and evt[2:0] = 0x001 (OR) results in 'no change'").
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.3 ("A request with data “0x0000 0000” and evt[2:0] = 0x001 (OR) results in “no change”"), TC18.txt L4889

requirements.title: GpioWriteSemantics' eight evt[2:0] codes are the endpoint's complete write surface
requirements.text: GpioWriteSemantics models exactly the eight evt[2:0] codes TC18 §13.7.4.1 defines for GPIO, with no ninth duration-carrying operation, matching the section's explicit statement that "Generating a pulse for a defined time is NOT a function of the GPIO endpoint" -- pulse generation is the Client's responsibility via two commands, a compound, or a trigger operation.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.1 ("Generating a pulse for a defined time is NOT a function of the GPIO endpoint"), TC18.txt L4811

requirements.title: GpioWriteSemantics::And follows Table 30's AND definition over §13.7.4.1's contradictory NAND wording
requirements.text: GpioWriteSemantics::And (evt[2:0]=010b) implements bitwise AND of byte_msg_payload with the current interface status, per TC18 §13.5 Table 30's normative per-endpoint evt table and its worked example ("with a byte_msg_payload of 0xFFFF FFFE the first IO pin will be reset, while other IO pins remain unchanged"); TC18 §13.7.4.1's prose instead says "NAND", a TC18-internal inconsistency this crate resolves in Table 30's favor rather than implementing as literally written.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("010b: The 'byte_msg_payload' bitwise AND 'current interface status' is written to the interface (example: with a byte_msg_payload of 0xFFFF FFFE the first IO pin will be reset, while other IO pins remain unchanged)") -- note: this crate's own text/doc-comments call this "Table 30", a stale table number from an earlier TC18 revision; the current TC18.txt (RC5) numbers it Table 33 (Table 30 is now "Error codes in responses", §12.9.6), TC18.txt L4098-4101

requirements.title: I2cSpeedMode::to_u8 encodes each speed preset as its i2c_mode wire byte
requirements.text: I2cSpeedMode::to_u8 encodes each of the five I2C speed presets (including the two adjacent high-speed rows this crate's spec-extraction pass could not distinguish) as its i2c_mode wire byte value 0..=4.

requirements.title: I2cSpeedMode::from_u8 rejects any byte outside 0..=4 without panicking
requirements.text: I2cSpeedMode::from_u8 returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) for any byte outside 0..=4, matching SpiChannelSelect::from_sub_opcode's own range-check discipline; never panics for any input.

requirements.title: I2cByteTransfer::encode emits bytes unmodified and unframed
requirements.text: I2cByteTransfer::encode returns the transfer's raw bytes (address byte(s) included) unmodified and unframed, with no bytes inserted, removed, or reordered.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.7.3 Figure 30 ("i2c request format"), TC18.txt L5240-5257

requirements.title: ISELED command payload is emitted verbatim with no inserted CRC
requirements.text: ISELED command encoding emits byte_msg_payload verbatim, in supplied order, with nothing inserted -- in particular no CRC -- per TC18 §13.7.12.3 (TC18.txt:5578, "plain data in the byte_msg_payload that is to be presented ... on the ISELED bus") and TC18.txt:5595's confirmation that no CRC is present on the ISELED network unless the endpoint is configured to generate one.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.12.3 ("In case of safe-operation mode a CRC will be added, that is not present on the ISELED network."), TC18.txt L6001-6003

requirements.title: IseledRequest enumerates the decoded shape of a Row-2 ISELED request after evt[2:0] validation, wrapping an already-decoded IseledFrame
requirements.text: IseledRequest's two variants (Plain(IseledFrame), ConfigWrite) give an incoming ISELED request's decoded shape after its evt.sub_opcode has been validated against evt_row2_kind_of's Table 33 Row-2 rule; IseledRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode is the request-decode entry point that performs that validation and dispatch. Unlike I2cRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode/LinRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode/AdcRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode/PwmInRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode/UartRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode (each of which take raw byte_msg_payload bytes and decode them internally), IseledRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode takes an already-decoded IseledFrame, matching CanRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode's own shape rather than those five siblings' -- IseledFrame already has its own dedicated decode entry point (IseledFrame::decode / IseledFrame::decode_line, both pre-existing this item and unchanged by it), so this evt[2:0]-classification entry point does not re-derive that byte-layout logic a second time internally
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33's Row-2 row (ISELED is one of its eight endpoint types), TC18.txt L4085-4092, and §13.7.12.3 ISELED EP request handling, TC18.txt L5578-5588

requirements.title: IseledRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode accepts Plain, rejects Reserved sub_opcodes with UnsupportedCmd, and rejects ConfigWrite with ConfigWriteNotImplemented, never panicking
requirements.text: IseledRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode wraps the caller-supplied IseledFrame unchanged in IseledRequest::Plain for a Plain (sub_opcode 0) request. Every Reserved sub_opcode value (evt[2:0] in 001b..=110b, or any value outside the 3-bit field's representable range) returns Err(RcpError::UnsupportedCmd), matching TC18 Table 33's Row-2 error-code requirement and every prior Row-2 endpoint-type module's identical refusal of their own table's reserved code. A ConfigWrite (sub_opcode 7) request returns Err(RcpError::ConfigWriteNotImplemented) rather than Ok(IseledRequest::ConfigWrite) -- following crate::can::CanRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode's own v5.8.0 departure from the Ok(Self::ConfigWrite) precedent I2C/LIN/ADC/PWM_IN/UART otherwise share, for the identical structural reason: from_evt_sub_opcode requires its caller to supply an already-decoded IseledFrame before this function is even called, and a genuine TC18 §12.7.1 config-write payload cannot be honestly decoded into one via IseledFrame::decode. See REQ-ISELED-012 and crate::iseled's own doc comment 'Provenance note: evt[2:0] request validation' for the full reasoning. Never panics for any sub_opcode/frame combination
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("000b to 110b reserved – request to be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD" / "111b: ... used to change the configuration of the endpoint (see 12.7.1)"), TC18.txt L4085-4092

requirements.title: RcServerState::INITIAL defaults to HwUnconfigured absent stored configuration
requirements.text: RcServerState::INITIAL is HwUnconfigured, the no-stored-configuration fallback TC18 §12.3 (TC18.txt:2059) describes: "After a power cycle or restart ... the RC Server shall start in the life-cycle state it is actually configured in", with a device having no NVM permitted to "incorporate default settings which allow it to be also starting in an advanced state".
requirements.tc18: §12.3 ("After a power cycle or restart ... the RC Server shall start in the life-cycle state it is actually configured in"), TC18.txt L2434-2437

requirements.title: is_transition_defined excludes the direct HW_UNCONFIGURED-to-RCP_CONFIGURED jump
requirements.text: is_transition_defined(HwUnconfigured, RcpConfigured) is false: TC18 §12.3.1.1 (TC18.txt:2168) states a request to advance directly from HW_UNCONFIGURED to RCP_CONFIGURED "will be rejected with an error response" -- the two-hop route through HW_CONFIGURED is the only defined path.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("A request to advance the state directly to RCP_CONFIGURED will be rejected with an error response."), TC18.txt L2544

requirements.title: LinFrameTransfer::encode emits the PID byte plus data unmodified and unframed
requirements.text: LinFrameTransfer::encode emits the PID byte followed by data, unmodified and unframed, matching TC18 §13.7.10.3 (TC18.txt:5304)'s description of byte_msg_payload as "the payload to be used on the Lin bus", with nothing inserted, removed, or reordered.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.10.3 Figure 39 ("lin request format"), TC18.txt L5719-5736

requirements.title: select_header_variant discards any frame that is neither NTSCF nor TSCF
requirements.text: select_header_variant accepts only the two AVTP subtypes RCP itself defines -- NTSCF (0x82) and TSCF (0x05) -- and discards every other leading subtype octet without attempting to interpret the following bytes, per the general AVTP discard rule ("If neither a gPTP nor an IEEE1722 frame is found the received frame shall be discarded").
requirements.tc18: §12.8.2 ("If neither a gPTP nor an IEEE1722 frame is found the received frame shall be discarded."), TC18.txt L3567

requirements.title: This crate assembles only NTSCF frames; no encode_tscf_frame counterpart exists
requirements.text: encode_ntscf_frame has no encode_tscf_frame counterpart: encode_tscf_header exists only for a client's own use and for round-trip testing, but nothing in this crate assembles a TSCF-headed frame, per TC18 §11.4.3 (TC18.txt:1988, "The RC Server always uses NTSCF header").
requirements.tc18: §11.4.3 ("TSCF headers will only be sent by RC Clients, never by the RC Servers. The RC Server always uses NTSCF header and only uses message_timestamp in ACF_GBB to convey a capture timestamp."), TC18.txt L2354-2355

requirements.title: resolve_pwm_in_read returns NoSignal once the configured timeout elapses, regardless of stale data
requirements.text: resolve_pwm_in_read returns Some(PwmInReadResolution::NoSignal) once elapsed_since_last_edge reaches config.no_signal_timeout, regardless of last_measured -- a stale measurement is never returned past the timeout; returns None only while still genuinely awaiting a first edge before the timeout, with the caller polling rather than this function blocking. Never panics for any input.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.6.2 Table 48 ("0b: if MAX PERIOD is exceeded, invalidate measurement and wait for new active phase of signal"), TC18.txt L5129-5135

requirements.title: PwmInRequest enumerates the decoded shape of a Row-2 PWM_IN request after evt[2:0] validation
requirements.text: PwmInRequest's two variants (Plain(PwmInByteTransfer), ConfigWrite) give an incoming PWM_IN request's decoded shape after its evt.sub_opcode has been validated against evt_row2_kind_of's Table 33 Row-2 rule; PwmInRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode is the request-decode entry point that performs that validation and dispatch. Unlike AdcRequest::Plain, which carries no payload struct at all because TC18 §13.7.9.3 states the ADC request has none, PwmInRequest::Plain carries a PwmInByteTransfer of the request's raw byte_msg_payload bytes, since TC18 §13.7.6.3 states the PWM_IN request (like its response) contains a byte_msg_payload of two 16-bit values -- but that payload is carried raw and undecoded rather than as a structured period/active-duration pair, since neither PwmDurationPair's own wire-level width/framing (already flagged unconfirmed in pwm.rs's own 'Provenance note: field widths and units') nor the request's own two-value meaning (TC18 §13.7.6.3 states only what the response's two values mean) is confirmed; mirrors I2cByteTransfer's identical unclear-framing discipline
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33's Row-2 row (PWM_IN is one of its eight endpoint types), TC18.txt L4085-4092, and §13.7.6.3 PWM_IN EP request handling ("The PWM_IN request and response contain two 16 bit values in the payload."), TC18.txt L5168-5170

requirements.title: PwmInRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode accepts Plain/ConfigWrite and rejects Reserved sub_opcodes with UnsupportedCmd, never panicking
requirements.text: PwmInRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode decodes a Plain (sub_opcode 0) request's payload bytes as a PwmInByteTransfer via PwmInByteTransfer::decode, recognizes a ConfigWrite (sub_opcode 7) request without attempting to interpret its payload (full TC18 §12.7.1 config-write payload decoding is deferred, not silently guessed at), and returns Err(RcpError::UnsupportedCmd) for every Reserved sub_opcode value, matching TC18 Table 33's Row-2 error-code requirement and crate::i2c::I2cRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode's/crate::adc::AdcRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode's identical refusal of their own table's reserved code; never panics for any sub_opcode/payload combination
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("000b to 110b reserved – request to be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD" / "111b: ... used to change the configuration of the endpoint (see 12.7.1)"), TC18.txt L4085-4092

requirements.title: build_error_response reuses the request's evt nibble verbatim, including evt[3]
requirements.text: build_error_response copies the originating request's evt field verbatim (via build_response_info), including evt[3] (the acknowledge-request bit) -- a known gap, since TC18 §11.3.4 (TC18.txt:1904) additionally requires an error response to carry evt[3:0] < 0x9, and this function does not enforce that bound (tracked further as REQ-RESP-007).
requirements.tc18: §11.3.4 ("With evt[3:0] < 0x9 and err = 1 the response is an error-response indicating that the execution of the request failed."), TC18.txt L2299-2301

requirements.title: build_error_response never sets message_timestamp on the error response
requirements.text: build_error_response never populates a message_timestamp on the response it builds, since this crate has no capture-timestamp source to supply one from.
requirements.tc18: §11.4.2 ("When timestamping was not requested, then the ACF_ABB type format without time stamp shall be default for any data transmitted by the RC Server."), TC18.txt L2340

requirements.title: HwPinMappingEntry::ENCODED_LEN is 3 bytes per Table 19's row stride
requirements.text: HwPinMappingEntry::ENCODED_LEN is 3, matching TC18 Table 19's row stride as fixed by IO_Pin 2's hw_ep_nr field at relative address 0x0003 -- hw_ep_nr, hw_ep_pin_nr, and hw_pin_type (undecomposed) each occupy one byte.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 Table 21 ("HW_config"), TC18.txt L3088-3108

requirements.title: ResponseStreamConfigEntry::ENCODED_LEN is 10 bytes per Table 24's row stride
requirements.text: ResponseStreamConfigEntry::ENCODED_LEN is 10, matching TC18 Table 24's row stride as fixed by Responder Queue 2's STREAM_UID field at relative address 0x000A.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.9 Table 27 ("Responder QUEUE_config"), TC18.txt L3421-3444

requirements.title: SequencerState mirrors SequencerStateEntry::seq_state's single-byte shape
requirements.text: SequencerState wraps a single u8, mirroring crate::regmap::SequencerStateEntry::seq_state's own single-byte shape -- this crate does not yet read this value from an actual register (see the module's own provenance note on the not-yet-built sequencer-state machine).
requirements.tc18: §12.7.10 Table 28 ("Seq_state: 8bit, current state"), TC18.txt L3473-3493

requirements.title: AvtpTimestamp::ROLLOVER_PERIOD is 2^32 nanosecond-ticks (~4.295s)
requirements.text: AvtpTimestamp::ROLLOVER_PERIOD is 1u64<<32, matching TC18 §11.4.1 (TC18.txt:1952-1953): "avtp_timestamp = (AS_sec x 10^9 + AS_ns) mod 2^32 ... thus rolls over every 4 seconds" -- ticks are nanoseconds and the modulus is the field's full 32-bit width (4.294967296s at 1ns/tick). The gPTP-derivation half of this same clause is a separate, unimplemented gap tracked as REQ-TIME-004.
requirements.tc18: §11.4.1 ("avtp_timestamp = (AS_sec × 10^9 + AS_ns) mod 2^32 where AS_sec is the gPTP seconds field and AS_ns is the gPTP nanoseconds field (thus rolls over every 4 seconds)") -- note: this requirement's own text and src/timestamp.rs's doc comment both cite this exact clause at a stale TC18.txt line number (L1952-1953); the correct location in the current TC18.txt (RC5) is TC18.txt L2328-2329

requirements.title: request_sleep_via_sleep_cmd only reaches sleep once all EPs are idle and responder queues are empty
requirements.text: request_sleep_via_sleep_cmd delegates to try_enter_power_mode, which admits the transition only when both PowerModeGateInput flags hold -- so a SleepCMD reaches sleep mode only once all EPs are idle and the responder queues are empty (all responses sent), per TC18 §13.7.2.3's third sleep-sequence step.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.3 ("3. as soon as all EPs are idle and the responder queues are empty (all responses sent): send an acknowledge to sleep request; bring the RC Server implementation to sleep mode."), TC18.txt L4548-4555

requirements.title: ByteMessageInfo::response_kind classifies per TC18 Table 15
requirements.text: ByteMessageInfo::response_kind() shall return ResponseKind::Acknowledge whenever evt.raw_nibble() equals 0xF, regardless of err or op, per TC18 Table 15/§11.3.1 -- a rejected Acknowledge (err=true) is still an Acknowledge, not a ResponseKind::Error. Otherwise it shall return ResponseKind::Error whenever err is true, and otherwise ResponseKind::Write when op is true or ResponseKind::Read.

requirements.title: I2cRequest enumerates the decoded shape of a Row-2 I2C request after evt[2:0] validation
requirements.text: I2cRequest's two variants (Plain(I2cByteTransfer), ConfigWrite) give an incoming I2C request's decoded shape after its evt.sub_opcode has been validated against evt_row2_kind_of's Table 33 Row-2 rule; I2cRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode is the request-decode entry point that performs that validation and dispatch
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33's Row-2 row (I2C is one of its eight endpoint types), TC18.txt L4085-4092, and §13.7.7.3 I2C EP request handling, TC18.txt L5240-5242

requirements.title: I2cRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode accepts Plain/ConfigWrite and rejects Reserved sub_opcodes with UnsupportedCmd, never panicking
requirements.text: I2cRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode decodes a Plain (sub_opcode 0) request's payload bytes as an I2cByteTransfer via I2cByteTransfer::decode, recognizes a ConfigWrite (sub_opcode 7) request without attempting to interpret its payload (full TC18 §12.7.1 config-write payload decoding is deferred, not silently guessed at), and returns Err(RcpError::UnsupportedCmd) for every Reserved sub_opcode value, matching TC18 Table 33's Row-2 error-code requirement and crate::gpio::apply_gpio_write's identical refusal of its own table's reserved code; never panics for any sub_opcode/payload combination
